_notes: Hand-curated overrides applied ON TOP of data/rolling-stock.json by scripts/build-locomotive-data.mjs. rolling-stock.json is a raw spreadsheet export and is overwritten wholesale whenever the sheet is re-exported, so anything curated by hand has to live here or it is lost on the next export. Keyed by section name -> class value (both exactly as they appear in rolling-stock.json). SEEDED 2026-08-04 from the 22 rows where the previous hand-maintained site-data.json had already diverged from the export: all 22 were Wikimedia 'File:' links replacing the export's less precise 'Category:' links. Those 22 were the ONLY divergence between the two files - every other field matched exactly. This file is also the intended home for the per-image attribution fields (photographer, license, sourceUrl) that Prompt B will add; the build script already passes unknown keys through to the class object, so adding them here needs no script change. 2026-08-04 additions: `corrections` (field-level data fixes) and `mergeDuplicates` (structural de-duplication of the same real-world class recorded twice under different key formats). Both are applied by the build script AFTER the raw export is read, so a re-export cannot silently undo them. 2026-08-04 (second pass): the remaining three known duplicate pairs (345/378/710) were merged on the same pattern as 777, and `additions` was added for classes that do not exist in the export at all — new rows have to live here rather than in rolling-stock.json, which is overwritten wholesale on re-export.

801.traction: Electric 25kV AC (auxiliary diesel engine fitted for emergency use only — not a bi-mode train)
801._why: Export said 'Bi-mode (25kV AC + diesel)', copying the 800/802 platform's traction value. The 801 is the electric-only IEP variant — Wikipedia's own infobox states explicitly 'not a bi-mode train'. It does carry one MTU 12V 1600 R80L diesel engine per unit, but strictly as emergency get-you-home backup, never for scheduled diesel-mode running the way the true bi-mode 800/802 are. This already matched the row's own Notes ('Electric-only variant of IEP') — only the traction column itself was inconsistent with it. FLAGGED separately (not changed here, scope was traction only): maxSpeedMph on this row is 140, but 140 is the IEP platform's design maximum — Wikipedia gives the 801's actual in-service/certified top speed as 125 mph, which is also what this dataset's own 802 row already uses for the same physical platform. Worth a second correction pass if confirmed.

802._why: Requested fix: remove 'Castle' — confirmed it is GWR's own name for its refurbished Class 43 HST sets (each power car nameplated after a Cornish castle, tradition retired Dec 2025), not for the 802. Applied exactly as scoped (Castle removed only). FLAGGED, not changed: 'Azuma' is ALSO misattributed here and was left in place because the request scoped this to Castle only — Azuma is exclusively LNER's brand, and this row's own `operators` field already lists the 802's real operators as 'Great Western Railway; TransPennine Express; Hull Trains' with no LNER at all (LNER's IEP units are 800/801/803, not 802). GWR's actual public brand for its 802 fleet is 'Intercity Express Train (IET)', already correctly named in this row's own `primaryService` field. Recommend replacing 'Azuma' with 'IET' in a follow-up pass if confirmed — proposed corrected value: 'IET / Nova 1 / Paragon (bi-mode)', matching all three real operator brands and dropping the two that don't belong (Azuma=LNER/801, Castle=GWR/Class 43).

345.notes: 70 nine-car trains in service. A June 2024 Alstom order (£370m / €430m) added 10 more, taking the eventual fleet to 80; production began October 2025 at Derby Litchurch Lane Works, the first unit (345071) completed and started testing in June 2026, and all ten are planned in service by 2027. Central section through London opened May 2022 (Crossrail). Capacity 1,500 total per train (454 seated, 1,046 standing).
345.numberBuilt: 70 in service; 10 more under construction (fleet reaching 80 by 2027)
345._why: REFINED 2026-08-15 on top of the 2026-08-04 correction below — that pass got the 70-vs-80 fact right but the capacity figure was left as an approximate '~1,500' and the in-progress order was described only vaguely ('being built... in testing at the time of writing'). Re-verified against Wikipedia's British Rail Class 345 infobox and Alstom/RailAdvent/Insider Media coverage of the June 2026 rollout: exact capacity is 1,500 total (454 seated, 1,046 standing) per nine-car unit, so the '~' is dropped. Order timeline confirmed precisely: signed June 2024 (£370m/€430m, both figures appear across sources for the same contract), production started October 2025, first unit 345071 rolled off the line and began test-track running in June 2026, remaining nine scheduled through 2026–2027, full batch in service by 2027 — not 'later this year' as one single article claimed for the whole order (that applies only to unit 345071). PRIOR _why (2026-08-04, retained for history): "CORRECTS THIS FILE'S OWN EARLIER CORRECTION. The export's commuter Notes said '80 nine-car trains' and the first pass treated that as an error against the duplicate metro row's '70', because the two rows contradicted each other. Verification shows BOTH were right about different things: 70 were built for the opening fleet, and a June 2024 Alstom order for 10 more takes it to 80. So the original 80 was a forward-looking figure, not a mistake."

Sheffield Supertram — Siemens-Duewag.cityNetwork: South Yorkshire Supertram (also known as Sheffield Supertram)
Sheffield Supertram — Siemens-Duewag._why: CORRECTS THIS FILE'S OWN EARLIER CORRECTION (was: 'Sheffield Supertram', set 2026-08-04). That pass normalised away 'South Yorkshire Supertram' as an ambiguous duplicate of 'Sheffield Supertram'. Re-checked 2026-08-15: the two are not interchangeable duplicates, they're two names for the same network from different eras, and which one is 'current' has flipped. At opening in 1994 the operator was South Yorkshire Supertram Limited (a SYPTE subsidiary). From the 1997 Stagecoach takeover through 2024 the network traded as Stagecoach Supertram and was popularly known as Sheffield Supertram. On 22 March 2024 it returned to public ownership under the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority, operated by South Yorkshire Future Trams Ltd, and the OFFICIAL name reverted to South Yorkshire Supertram — this matches the current Wikipedia article title and the operator's own branding (its X/Twitter account is @SY_Supertram, bio 'South Yorkshire's Transport'). 'Sheffield Supertram' has NOT gone fully historical though — regional press (e.g. The Star) is still using it in 2026 headlines — so this is recorded as 'also known as', not 'formerly'. There is no separate, distinct 'Sheffield Supertram' entity today; it's the same network as South Yorkshire Supertram. Both rows tied to this network (this one and the Class 399 addition) now carry the identical base network-name string again, for the same reason the 2026-08-04 pass cared about it: naming-based counts should see one network, not two.

34067.notes: Two Battle of Britain-class Bulleid Pacifics currently run: Tangmere (built Brighton Works 1947), owned by the Tangmere Locomotive Company and operated by West Coast Railway Company, frequently works the Golden Arrow and other Pullman-style excursions; City of Wells (built Brighton Works 1949), based with East Lancashire Railway, is a regular mainline performer.
34067._why: Folds the individually-named 34067 'Tangmere' and 34092 'City of Wells' rows into one plain class-level row, matching the existing bare-class-number pattern already used elsewhere in this same section (20/37/47/57 — a bare class number with a family/group name, no individual loco name in that cell) rather than inventing a new row-grouping pattern. Both engines' individual names are preserved in the notes text rather than dropped. 34092's row is removed via mergeDuplicates below; this correction retargets 34067's own class/name/notes and merges the two rows' operators and primaryService into one combined description, since the two source rows disagreed on both (Tangmere: Tangmere Locomotive Co/WCRC, mainline railtours; City of Wells: ELR, heritage tours) and the instruction did not specify field-by-field merge mechanics — flagged for review if a different treatment (e.g. picking one operator only) is preferred. yearIntro is the two specific engines' own build years (1947, 1949), not the wider Battle of Britain subclass's historical build range.

mergeDuplicates._why: Same real-world class recorded twice under different key formats. The Commuter row is kept as home because its bare class value '777' produces the canonical anchor fleet-777, which map.html's Fleet chips link to; the metro row's anchor (fleet-class-777-merseyrail) is targeted by nothing. The metro row's fleetSize and cityNetwork are merged in rather than dropped — the unified schema holds both those and the commuter row's operators/primaryService, so nothing is lost. The 777 is then cross-listed into `metro` via CROSS_LISTINGS, which is what the duplicate row was hand-approximating before categories[] existed.

Same class, two rows. Commuter row kept as home so the fleet-345 anchor survives. NOTE two real disagreements between the pair, both flagged in the report: (1) traction — commuter said 'Electric 25kV AC', metro said 'Dual-voltage (25kV AC / 750V DC)'. The Elizabeth line is 25kV AC throughout with no third-rail running, so the commuter value is correct and is the one kept (the merge only fills EMPTY fields, so the wrong metro value is discarded rather than picked). (2) fleet count — the commuter Notes said '80 nine-car trains' while the metro Fleet Size said '70'. 70 is correct; the notes are corrected below.

Same class, two rows. No factual disagreement — traction, builder, year and speed matched exactly; the two Notes were complementary rather than contradictory. The metro row's note ('East London Line, North London Line, West London Line. Dual-voltage for AC and DC sections.') is discarded with the row; its content is already carried by the kept row's primaryService and traction fields.

Same class, two rows. Traction differed only by a trailing space, which the build script's clean() already strips — not a real conflict. One editorial error found and DISCARDED WITH THE ROW rather than merged: the metro note said 'DC-only routes', which contradicts both its own dual-voltage traction field and the 25kV AC Gospel Oak-Barking route the same row lists. Flagged in the report; no correction needed because the note does not survive the merge.

Folds 34092 'City of Wells' into the retargeted 34067 row (corrected above to bare class '34', name 'SR Battle of Britain'). No mergeFields needed — the kept row's class/name/operators/primaryService/notes were already rewritten by the 34067 correction to cover both engines, so there is nothing left on the removed row to pull across. This is the first use of mergeDuplicates for two DIFFERENT source class numbers folding into a THIRD, renamed class value, rather than a same-class-different-key-format dedupe — the keep-side correction runs first (pass 1) and changes 34067's own `class` field to '34' before this merge (pass 1b) looks it up, which is why `keep.class` here is '34' and not '34067'.
